newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX ends steady, trendless trade seen.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX ends steady, trendless trade seen.

text.p: The BUX index finished virtually steady in a mixed market on Monday, foreshadowing days of trendless trade, with little impact expected from a potential U.S. rate change this week, traders said.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 6,795.00 points up 10.34, but below a new trading peak of 6,814.22 points.

"There was a day (recently) when the Dow fell 2.5 percent and Budapest rose 1.5 percent, so I don't necessarily say there would be any link between the two markets," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities.
"Perhaps a time is coming when prices stop rocketing and leave opportunities for investors to buy shares at lower prices," he said. "I expect the market to remain at around the current index level."
James Oates, Director for Central and Eastern Europe at UBS, added he expected Hungarian prices to drift sideways.
"I suspect that people will prefer to stick with the relatively lower risks of Hungary but I don't believe that people really want to add," he said.
On Monday, two of the market's top recent gainers, oil firm MOL and chemicals, declined, while OTP Bank and pharmaceuticals Richter continued their bull run.

"I had the feeling there were investors who closed arbitrage positions (between the cash and futures market) but, unlike earlier, they did not sell at whatever price, so they did not push prices substantially lower," Berecz said.
OTP finished at 5,000 forints, down 50, after rising to a new peak of 5,080. Richter ended at 17,245 forints, up 245, after it also set a new record high of 17,500.
Retailer Fotex finished at 209 forints, down 11, after oscillating between 196 and 220 forints.
